inventedEvidence.evidence: 'because the water has reached your plug sockets and extension lead' - customer only said water was 'spreading toward an extension lead' and the socket is at worktop height

rationale: The assistant handled the critical hazard correctly: immediate stop-use, do not touch wet plug/socket/lead, isolate at the consumer unit, and it confirmed this when the customer asked. It correctly confirmed the washing-up-liquid cause once the customer volunteered it, though its own first question (standing water in the base) was less relevant than asking about detergent. It overstated the evidence by saying water had 'reached' the sockets and lead, and the escalation was vague and somewhat excessive (generic 'qualified engineer' before any reuse, rather than an electrician only for the wet lead/socket, plus informing the landlord), and it never got to the practical suds-clearing steps.
